definitions.gloss: to hone, to sharpen, to refine
definitions.explanation: To sharpen something to a fine, keen edge. Most commonly used figuratively for sharpening senses, sensibilities, skills, or awareness to an extremely high degree.

examples.japanese: {神経|しんけい}を{研|と}ぎ{澄|す}ます。
{研|と}ぎ{澄|す}まされた{感覚|かんかく}で{音|おと}を{聞|き}き{分|わ}ける。
examples.english: To distinguish sounds with sharpened senses.

examples.japanese: {長年|ながねん}の{経験|けいけん}で{研|と}ぎ{澄|す}まされた{職人|しょくにん}の{技|わざ}は、{見|み}る{者|もの}を{圧倒|あっとう}する。
examples.english: The craftsman's skill, honed through years of experience, overwhelms those who watch.

notes:
USAGE:
Almost always used figuratively in modern Japanese. The passive form {研|と}ぎ{澄|す}まされた (honed, refined) is very common as a modifier: {研|と}ぎ{澄|す}まされた{感性|かんせい} (refined sensibility), {研|と}ぎ{澄|す}まされた{神経|しんけい} (sharpened nerves). Conveys a sense of extreme refinement through effort or experience.

WRITING:
{研|と}ぐ means "to polish" or "to sharpen" and {澄|す}ます means "to make clear/pure." Together they convey the idea of sharpening something to crystalline clarity.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {神経|しんけい}を{研|と}ぎ{澄|す}ます: to sharpen one's nerves
- {感覚|かんかく}を{研|と}ぎ{澄|す}ます: to hone one's senses
- {研|と}ぎ{澄|す}まされた{感性|かんせい}: refined sensibility
- {研|と}ぎ{澄|す}まされた{美|うつく}しさ: a keen, refined beauty
